FOREWORD 


This Indian Standard [P : 94] (First Revision) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards on recommendation 
of the Methods of Sampling and Test for Petroleum, its Products, Gaseous Fuels and Lubricants Sectional 
Committee and approval of the Petroleum, Coal and Related Products Division Council. 


This standard was initially published in 1980, which was based on the joint publication No. ASTM D 942-78 and 
IP Designation 142/74. 


In this revision revision considerable assistance has been derived from ASTM D 942-15. Title of the standard is 
modified and new reagents used for testing were included. This test method measures the net change in pressure 
resulting from consumption of oxygen by oxidation and gain in pressure due to formation of volatile oxidation by- 
products. This test method may be used for quality control to indicate batch-to-batch uniformity. It also predicts 
neither the stability of greases under dynamic service conditions, nor the stability of greases stored in containers 
for long periods, nor the stability of films of greases on bearings and motor-parts. It should not be used to estimate 
the relative oxidation resistance of different grease types. 


In reporting the results of a test or analysis made in accordance with this standard, if the final value, observed or 
calculated, is to be rounded off, it shall be done in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 ‘Rules for rounding off numerical 
values (revised y. 


IS 1448 [P : 94] : 2019 


Indian Standard 


METHODS OF TEST FOR 
PETROLEUM AND ITS PRODUCTS 
[P : 94] 


TEST FOR OXIDATION STABILITY OF LUBRICATING 
GREASE BY OXYGEN PRESSURE VESSEL METHOD 


( First Revision ) 


1 SCOPE 


This standard [P : 94] describes the method of 
test for determination of resistance of lubricating 
greases to oxidation when stored statically in an 
oxygen atmosphere in a sealed system at an elevated 
temperature under conditions of test. 


WARNING — This standard may involve hazardous 
materials, operations and equipment. This standard 
does not purport to address all of the safety problems 
associated with its use. It is the responsibility of the 
user of this standard to establish appropriate safety 
and health practices and determine the applicability of 
regulatory limitations prior to use. 


2 REFERENCES 


The following standards contain provisions which, 
through reference in this text, constitute provisions 
of this standard. All standards are subject to revision, 
and parties to agreements based on this standard are 
encouraged to investigate the possibility of applying the 
most recent editions of the standards indicated below: 


IS No. 
6911 : 1992 


Title 


Stainless steel plate, sheet and strip 


3 OUTLINE OF THE METHOD 


The sample of grease is oxidized in a pressure vessel 
heated to 99°C and filled with oxygen at 758 kPa. 
The degree of oxidation at a given period of time is 
determined by the corresponding decrease in oxygen 
pressure which is observed at regular intervals. 


4 APPARATUS 


4.1 Oxidation Pressure Vessel 


Conforming to the dimensions shown in Fig. 1, shall be 
made of 18 percent chromium, 8 percent nickel alloy 
steel. A suitable material is an alloy steel conforming 
to Grade S, Type 304 / 304 L of IS 6911. The pressure 
vessel shall be capable of withstanding a working 
pressure of 1241 kPa at 99°C and provided with a lead 


or TFE- fluorocarbon gasket for sealing. The interior 
surfaces of the pressure vessel, the lid, and the inside 
of the pipe shall be well polished. The volume of the 
pressure vessel shall be 185 + 6 ml, when measured 
to the level of the gauge. A screw-on lid may be used 
instead of the bolt-on lid shown in Fig. 1. 


4.2 Pressure Gauge 


Suitable for use with oxygen and mineral oil, which 

is of the indicating type, graduated in intervals of 

6.89 kPa per scale division, with a maximum reading 

of at least 827 kPa and capable of an accuracy of at 

least 3.45 kPa, within the interval 621 to 827 kPa. 

Attach the gauge to the stem as shown in Fig. 1. 
NOTE — A recording pressure gauge may be used in place 
of the prescribed indicating pressure gauge, if it satisfies the 
volume and accuracy requirements previously stated. 


4.3 Oil Bath 


Capable of being controlled at 99 + 0.5°C, with a 
temperature gradient less than 0.5°C in the body of the 
oil used and of sufficient depth to allow submersion 
of the pressure vessel to the proper depth. Circulation 
of the oil heating medium by a pump or stirring is 
recommended. Sufficient heat capacity shall be provided 
to return the bath to the required temperature within 
60 min after immersion of the pressure vessel. Provide 
the bath with a thermometer, such that the 96.8°C point 
of the thermometer is at the same level as the upper 
surface of the bath cover. Adjust the level of the bath 
so that the top of the pressure vessel is submerged 
approximately 50 mm below its surface. There shall be 
no drafts or wide fluctuations in temperature around the 
gauges in the bath. 


NOTE —— Other constant-temperature baths may be used 
if they are equivalent in heat capacity and thermal gradient 
characteristics to the oil bath described in the Annex and can 
be shown to maintain the pressure vessel at the prescribed test 
temperature. 


4.4 Dish Holder 


Constructed of 18 percent chromium, 8 percent nickel 
alloy steel as described for the oxidation pressure 
vessel, shall conform to the dimensions prescribed in 
Fig. 1.

Fic. 1 APPARATUS FOR OXIDATION STABILITY TEST OF LUBRICATING GREASES 


4.5 Sample Dishes 

Of glass conforming to the dimensions prescribed in 
Fig. 1. 

4.6 Thermometer 


Having a range of 95 to 103°C, accuracy to measure 
up to 0.1°C and shall comply with the following 
requirements: 


Range 95 to 103°C 
Graduation at each 0.1°C 
Immersion Total 
Overall length 280 mm 
Figured at each 1°C 

Top Finish Ring 

Scale error not to exceed +0.2°C 


NOTE — Thermometers conforming to ASTM 22C/IP 24C 
may be used. 


5 REAGENTS 


5.1 Oxygen, of not less than 99.5 percent purity. 
5.1.1 Caution 


Since oxygen vigorously accelerates combustion, 
observe the following procedures: 


a) Keep oil and grease away from oxygen at high 
pressure. Keep oil and grease away from all 
regulators, gages and control equipment. 


b) Use oxygen only with equipment conditioned for 
oxygen service by careful cleaning to remove oil 
and grease from area in contact with high pressure 
oxygen. 

c) Keep combustibles away from oxygen and 
eliminate ignition sources. 


d) Keep surfaces clean to prevent ignition or 
explosion, or both, upon contact with high 
pressure oxygen. 

e) Always use a pressure regulator to deliver oxygen. 
Release regulator tension before opening oxygen 
cylinder. 

f) All equipment used must be suitable and 
recommended for oxygen service. 

g) Never attempt to transfer oxygen from cylinder in 
which it is received to any other cylinder prior to 
use. 

h) Do not drop oxygen cylinders. 

j) Keep cylinder valve closed when not in use. 


k) Stand away from valve when opening cylinder. 


IS 1448 [P : 94] : 2019 


m) Do not breathe or use technical grade oxygen for 
inhalation purposes. 


n) See other literature for details of safe practice in 
the use of oxygen. 


5.2 n-Heptane 


WARNING — Flammable. Harmful if inhaled. Keep 
away from heat, sparks and open flame. Keep container 
closed. Use adequate ventilation. Avoid breathing 
vapor. Avoid prolonged or repeated skin contact. 


5.3 Cleaning Solution 


NOTE — Chromic acid cleaning solutions or equivalently 
strong oxidizing non-chromium containing acid can be used as 
cleaning solutions 


WARNING — Chromic acid cleaning solutions 
or strong oxidizing non chromium containing acid 
solutions may cause severe burns, can be carcinogenic, 
hygroscopic, can catch fire. Do not get it in eyes, on 
skin, or on clothing. Avoid breathing vapor. Do not take 
internally. 


6 PREPARATION OF APPARATUS 


Clean the sample dishes with n-heptane and then with 
a cleaning solution. Follow the final cleaning operation 
by a thorough tap water rinse, a distilled water rinse, 
and drying in an oven. 
NOTE — If lacquer is found after a run, clean the inside 
of the oxidation pressure vessel and the metal supports for 
the pressure vessel dishes by immersing in an appropriate 
solvent capable of removing the lacquer, such as gum solvent, 
scorching powder and scrubbing with a bristle brush followed 


by drying. 


WARNING — Handle in well-ventilated area, 
preferably in a hood. Keep away from heat, sparks and 
flame. Container to be closed when not in use. Avoid 
skin contact. Harmful if inhaled. 


7 PROCEDURE 


7.1 Fill each of the five dishes with 4.00 + 0.01 g 
of grease. Distribute the samples in the dishes in a 
uniform manner. Place the filled dishes on the five 
bottom shelves of the holder, leaving the top shelf to act 
as a cover to prevent condensing volatile products from 
dropping into the grease samples. When assembling the 
pressure vessel, place a small ball of glass wool in the 
bottom of the stem. 


7.2 Place the dish holder in the pressure vessel with a 
sealing gasket in place, and close the pressure vessel by 
tightening the bolts slowly and uniformly. Clear the air 
from the pressure vessel by introducing oxygen slowly 
until a pressure of 689 kPa is attained, then allow the 


IS 1448 [P : 94] : 2019 


oxygen to escape slowly; repeat four times. Bring the 
oxygen pressure to a value as shown in the following 
table: 


Room Temperature, °C Pressure, kPa 


17 to 20 586 
20 to 23 593 
23 to 27 600 
27 to 30 607 
30 to 33 614 
33 to 37 621 
37 to 40 627 


Allow the pressure vessel to stand overnight to make 
sure there are no leaks. 


NOTE — It was found that pressure readings as shown above 
will result in a pressure reading of 758 + 14 kPa, when the 
pressure vessel is placed in the bath in the following step, 7.3, 
and consequently no release of oxygen will be required in 
most cases. This minimizes the chance of a leak developing 
at the valve after the overnight check for leaks has shown the 
pressure vessel to be satisfactory. 


7.3 Place the pressure vessel in the oil bath maintained 
at a temperature of 99 + 0.5°C. As the pressure rises, if 
needed, intermittently release oxygen from the pressure 
vessel until a constant pressure of 758 + 14 kPa is 
obtained and maintained for at least 2 h. A gradual drop 
in pressure indicates a continuous leak in the pressure 
vessel. Observe and record the pressure at least every 
24 h. In case a leak develops, do not report the results 
but repeat the test. 


7.4 Start timing at the moment of immersion of 
the pressure vessel in the oil bath, and continue the 
oxidation for the time period specified. 

NOTE — Specifications are usually given in terms of pressure 


drop in kilopascals at one or more time intervals, for instance, 
after 100, 200 h, and so forth. 


8 REPORT 


Report the average of duplicate determinations as 
pressure drop in kilopascals for the specified test time, 
or times in hours. 


9 PRECISION AND BIAS 


9.1 The precision of this test method as determined by 
statistical examination of inter laboratory results is as 
follows: 


9.1.1 Repeatability 


The difference between two test results, obtained by the 
same operator with the same apparatus under constant 
operating conditions on identical test material would, 
in the long run, in the normal and correct operation of 
the test method, exceed the following values only in 
one case in twenty: 


Mean Pressure Drop, kPa Repeatability 
0 to 34.5 13.8 
Over 34.5 to 68.9 20.7 
Over 68.9 to 138 41.4 
Over 138 to 379 68.9 


9.1.2 Reproducibility — The difference between two 
single and independent results obtained by different 
operator’s working in different laboratories on identical 
test material would, in the long run, in the normal 
and correct operation of the test method, exceed the 
following values only in one case in twenty: 


Mean Pressure Drop, kPa Reproducibility 
0 to 34.5 20.7 
Over 34.5 to 68.9 34.5 
Over 68.9 to 138 55.2 
Over 138 to 379 138 


NOTE — These precision values apply only to that portion of 
the data for which oxygen is absorbed at a rate approximately 
proportional to time (for example, the induction period). The 
end of the induction period is evidenced by a rapid acceleration 
in the rate of oxygen absorption in a short time interval.
